items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: He won the singer away from I think Dick Haymes, whoever the other boy singer was.

ctx.x: We’re going to get to that. You kind of tweaked my memory before we started recording about the way things used to be. And you mentioned the ice man delivering ice and I was talking about the milkman. And just yesterday I was doing some research on something and I happened to look at the top popular songs of 1950. It makes me wonder, you would have been 15 years old at that time and I assume that you had started the trumpet?

Yes. I actually started when I was eleven. I went and saw a movie when I was in the seventh grade and it was Harry James, and he was the feature. He was the guy that was the focal point, and his band. And I remember Dick Haymes I think was in it and then a girl singer. And I went away wanting to play a trumpet because Harry was in front of the band playing. He won the singer away from I think Dick Haymes, whoever the other boy singer was. I went home and asked my dad, you know, if I could get a trumpet. So he…

good player, I was just in the ninth grade. So the high school in Riverside, there’s only one high school, Riverside Polytechnic High. And they had a great band and they had — there were three junior high schools that fed into the high school so they picked all three first chair junior high players to put in the advanced band. So I was next to last chair. And they were supposed to have a concert the next day at an elementary school, you know, a big thing for us. And so the trumpet player, the first trumpet…
